title: Why Are Some Lakes Pink and Turquoise?
script: Why is that lake bright pink? It is all because of tiny salt-loving algae and bacteria. When water evaporates and salt levels spike, these microscopic organisms produce a red pigment to protect themselves from harsh sunlight. Other lakes glow turquoise due to melting glaciers grinding rock into ultra-fine flour suspended in the water. Meanwhile, acidic volcanic lakes turn a striking emerald green from dissolved minerals. Nature simply uses chemistry as her paintbrush. Subscribe for more surprising science stories every week.
